clue.text: As is 'billet-dou' in 'a billet-doux'?

blocks.note: surface reading: a puzzle about how a French phrase is spelt
setter's reading: the letters billet-dou sit closed in between an A and an X, the crossword's kiss, just as a love letter is traditionally closed off

explanation.surface: A pedantic question about where a French love-letter phrase sits inside a longer phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: A billet-doux is a love letter. Inside 'a billet-doux' the core is wrapped by A at the front and X, the usual kiss symbol, at the back: closed up with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the customary sign-off pressed onto a love letter's envelope, describing how it was closed.

clue.text: Lido with black stripe, swimming pool

indicators.note: things that are swimming move about freely, so the preceding letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of an open-air lido with a black lane line painted along its swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like part of the lido scene, but it is the game played with cues on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket billiards is the American name for pool, the cue game where balls are sunk into table pockets.

clue.text: Conflict is over issue about which steps taken

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set over another simply sits above it, so the first comes before the second
about means surrounding, so the following piece wraps around the earlier ones

blocks.note: taken as written
a son is one's issue, or offspring
a dance is an activity in which steps are taken

explanation.surface: A dispute over some matter on which action has already been taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which steps taken' is a cryptic description of an activity done on foot to music, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissonance is discord or disagreement, a figurative sense from clashing musical notes.

clue.text: Resort where character took a deep breath, audibly?

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the letters are spelt the way the spoken words sound

blocks.note: a character is a letter, here C, whose name is said see
to sigh is to take a deep audible breath

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where a person in a story inhaled deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a story; here it is a letter of the alphabet, C, so 'C sighed' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town is a typical holiday resort by the coast.

clue.text: Study that's barely sufficient, curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: scant means barely enough

explanation.surface: A piece of research that only just passes muster, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to study or examine it closely, as a verb.

clue.text: Local favourite takes nothing from disappointing mark in college

indicators.note: takes, with from, means removing something from the word that follows
in means placed inside, so the mark sits within the college name

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a poor result is disappointing
a scratch is a mark on a surface
King's is a Cambridge college

explanation.surface: A popular pub figure scores a dismal zero mark at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; pork scratchings, crisp fried pork rind, are a classic pub snack. King's is a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork scratchings are a salty snack sold in bags at British pubs, a favourite at the local.

clue.text: Standing against British rule where one is stymied by parliament, is it an omnishambles?

indicators.note: stymied by means hemmed in by, so the single letter is trapped inside the longer word
an omnishambles is a total mess, so all the letters are jumbled up

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political question: does a lone figure blocked by parliament prove the system is a fiasco?
explanation.walkthrough: Omnishambles is a recent British coinage, from the TV satire The Thick of It, for a situation botched in every respect.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-imperialist opposes empire, such as Britain's rule over its colonies.

clue.text: Dress up as Satan, passing masks on

definitions.note: figurative: to portray someone as a devil

indicators.note: a mask covers something, so the outer word hides the short word inside it

blocks.note: passing is a euphemism for death, demise
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone putting on a devil costume while the face masks are handed along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up as Satan' reads like fancy dress; it means portraying someone as evil.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonise is to depict a person as a demon, wicked and threatening, in public portrayal.

clue.text: Those Charles has?

blocks.note: surface reading: a vague question about some man named Charles's possessions
setter's reading: Charles is the King, so what he owns as monarch are regal headpieces

explanation.walkthrough: Charles is King Charles III, who has several regal headpieces; the plural also hints at the old coins and at dental caps.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch possesses ceremonial headpieces worn at coronation and state occasions.

clue.text: See 22
Language teacher finally coming in naked?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
coming in means entering, so the letter goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: last letter of teacher
naked is without kit; sans is French for without

explanation.surface: A language tutor arrives at last wearing no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: SANS KIT, without clothes, takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the classical language of ancient India, used in Hindu scripture.

clue.text: Check articles etc. translated: Italian features

indicators.note: features means includes, so the letters are sitting within the words before it

blocks.note: the end of translated and the start of Italian

explanation.surface: A note that written pieces translated from Italian need looking over.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit articles is to check and correct pieces of writing before publication.

clue.text: Naughty pic with dustman where everything exposed

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters will not stay in their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky photo of a refuse collector somewhere nothing is kept covered.
explanation.walkthrough: A dustman is a British rubbish collector.
explanation.definitionFit: At a naturist resort, guests go without clothes, so all is on show.

clue.text: Elegant poet drank

blocks.note: Shakespeare is the Swan of Avon, so a swan can be a poet
to neck a drink is British slang for gulping it down

explanation.surface: A refined poet knocked back a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elegant poet' reads as one phrase; Elegant alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a long graceful neck like a swan suggests poise and grace.

clue.text: Indian dish I found beside one fed to no Messiah?

indicators.note: something fed to another goes into it, so the letter is put inside
beside means placed next to, so the pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: in Monty Python's Life of Brian, Brian is famously not the Messiah
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finding a mystery character next to a feeding not meant for a saviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy!' is the famous line from Life of Brian. B(I)RIAN then I.
explanation.definitionFit: Biriani is a spiced rice dish from Indian cuisine, here in one of its spellings.

clue.text: Middle Eastern food: some not quite in season for Americans

indicators.note: not quite means just short, so the final letter is dropped
in means placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a few is some
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A recipe note that some of this dish is almost in season in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Falafel are fried balls of ground chickpeas, a staple street food of the Levant.

clue.text: Nail in rising water wears away

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top
in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: the sea is a body of water
a brad is a thin small-headed nail

explanation.surface: A nail left in rising water slowly corrodes.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or erode a surface by friction.

clue.text: Cake: endless sweetener on the side

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the last letter goes
in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

blocks.note: Chelsea is a London football team, a side
a bung is a bribe, a sweetener

explanation.surface: A cake with a never-ending supply of sugar served alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests sugar; here it is a bribe. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a coiled currant-filled sweet bun, a classic British teatime bake.

clue.text: Bird unable to fly having lost right wing, dashing

indicators.note: the right wing of a word written across is its final letter, which is removed

blocks.note: a young bird too small to fly yet

explanation.surface: A flightless bird that has lost a wing, rushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' seems to describe the bird running; it means stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and smart, as dashing does of an elegant appearance.

clue.text: State where house secured by goodish priest?

indicators.note: something secured by another is held within it

blocks.note: OK means fair, reasonably good
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A place where a home is guarded by a fairly decent cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty US states, in the south-central region.

clue.text: Oh no ducks, I nearly forgot!

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
a postscript adds something the writer nearly forgot

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay at nearly forgetting the ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so it gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is an exclamation of dismay at a small mistake, like a rueful cry of alarm.

clue.text: Hot ingredient provided in cold water

indicators.note: in means placed inside the surrounding words

blocks.note: a chill is cold
if means provided that
lakes are bodies of water

explanation.surface: A spicy ingredient served up in icy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' and 'cold' sit side by side to set up a contrast; 'provided' looks like 'supplied' but is the conditional word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli flakes are dried crushed peppers used to add heat to food.

clue.text: Pseud sacked by bureau ultimately finished

indicators.note: sacked suggests being thrown out in disorder, so the letters get rearranged
ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of bureau

explanation.surface: A pretentious person fired from an office, and that's the end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A pseud is a pretentious poser, British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means exhausted or consumed, all gone and finished.

clue.text: Switch on back of appliance is green, possibly

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
possibly signals the words could be arranged another way

blocks.note: last letter of appliance
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that the power switch on the back of a machine may be eco-friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise a circuit is to supply it with power, turning it on.
